data.name: Stonehenge VR SANDBOX
data.detailed_description:
Hi Voyagers!

We'd love for you to check out our new VR game Alien Dawn.

Link is below and thank you!

Christian & Jessica





Stonehenge VR began its journey as a profound learning experience, enjoyed by thousands of families, when it originated as one of the first room scale VR exhibits on display in a museum. The first location was the Pacific Science Center in Seattle, Washington, and the second was the Museum at Prairiefire in Overland Park, Kansas.

The Museum Mode serves as a wonderful entry point for the first time VR user. Starting with a built in tutorial, it prepares people of all ages on how to interact in virtual reality.

This VR experience includes narrated voice overs, interactivity, and animations that will give you a new appreciation for its fascinating history and beauty as you travel to the world famous prehistoric monument in Wiltshire, England.



Designed to expand the experience for the home VR user, Stonehenge VR 2.0 with SANDBOX Mode puts minimal limitations on the creator allowing them to roam across the map and create virtual worlds on any scale desired.

Build, paint and knock down your own version of the Stonehenge monument with motion controllers in real time. Design your own ancient monument around the original Stonehenge, or delete it and start in an empty field.

The SANDBOX is user friendly for the beginner with many tools to discover, and three types of locomotion options for the more experienced VR user. Many additional pre-made monuments for you to explore come built in to the Stonehenge VR SANDBOX.



Share your Stonehenge VR SANDBOX Creations With Us!

Contact us by email or on social media and share images and/or videos of what you create! The founders, Christian and Jessica, would love to see what you’ve made with the Stonehenge VR SANDBOX.

Our favorites will be posted on our social media pages and even include your actual SANDBOX saved games in the application itself!

Stonehenge VR Museum Mode Features:
  • A profound learning experience of the Neolithic monument
  • Voice over guided tour of Stonehenge monument in Wiltshire England
  • Witness the Winter and Summer Solstice at different points in history
  • Watch the sunrise and set through the stones
  • English and Mandarin Chinese translations
  • Fully interactive
  • Virtual reality camera to save images of your creations
  • Created in the Unreal 4 Engine
VoyagerVR SANDBOX Features:
  • A physics based creation tool for all ages
  • Build own version of Neolithic monument using multiple rock models and sizes
  • Paint stones endless amount of times with eight color options
  • Knock down your own structures
  • Three locomotion options: Fly, walk or teleport to any location on map
  • Comes with pre-made monuments to explore
  • Save and share creations using the Rama Save System
  • Change the time of day on the fly
  • Music player with Stonehenge VR soundtrack, or custom music files
Supported Hardware:
  • HTC Vive - Room Scale
  • Oculus Rift / Touch - Room Scale
  • Windows Mixed Reality (Only with SteamVR Plugin)
  • Leap Motion - Hand Tracking
Unreal Plugins:
  • Nvidia VRWorks - Performance Increase
  • Nvidia Ansel - 360 Photo Export
  • Rama Save System - Save/Load SANDBOX Creations
  • Rama Victory Plugin - Save VR Photographs to JPG

The Developer:

After having his mind blown by VR in 2013, and seeing how the tech could be used for education, Christian Bretz decided to change careers and went looking for financing to start his first VR project. When he wasn't able to get the financing necessary to hire a developer, he decided to teach him self how to develop VR software in the Unreal Engine using tutorials and information he found online.

Three months later he created the first version of Stonehenge VR, and less than a year after that it became one of the first room scale VR exhibits to ever be displayed in a museum.

First was the Pacific Science Center in Seattle, WA, then the Museum at Prairiefire in Overland Park, KS. It also became a launch title for HTC’s Viveport and has been featured by many tech and media publications such as, CNet, Variety and VRScout.

Christian and his Co-Founder Jessica Villarreal design all the software, and run the business themselves all out of their home in Los Angeles, CA.

reviews.review:
Stonehenge VR SANDBOX offers an unusual blend of historical exploration, interactive education, and creative experimentation, transforming one of humanity's most mysterious prehistoric landmarks into an immersive virtual environment. Developed and published by VoyagerVR, the experience prioritizes curiosity and discovery over traditional gaming objectives. Instead of presenting combat encounters, complicated missions, or competitive challenges, it invites players to explore an ancient monument, understand its historical significance, and experiment with building their own stone formations. The result is an interesting virtual reality attraction that combines the atmosphere of a museum exhibit with the freedom of a construction sandbox, although its relatively modest gameplay depth limits its broader appeal.

The historical exploration component is arguably the strongest aspect of the experience. Museum Mode allows players to examine Stonehenge from perspectives that would be difficult or impossible to experience during an ordinary visit. The enormous standing stones become particularly impressive when viewed at their intended scale through a virtual reality headset. Guided narration introduces historical information about the monument, while environmental presentations demonstrate its relationship with astronomical events. Observing sunlight move across the ancient formations during seasonal demonstrations creates a memorable atmosphere and encourages appreciation for the engineering knowledge and cultural traditions of prehistoric societies. Although the educational content does not provide an exhaustive archaeological investigation, it communicates its subject matter in an accessible and engaging manner.

What makes the experience more interesting than a conventional virtual museum is the inclusion of a dedicated sandbox environment. Players can manipulate individual stones, rearrange existing formations, and construct entirely new monuments using the available building pieces. This creative freedom encourages experimentation with different architectural arrangements, whether attempting to reproduce recognizable prehistoric structures or inventing something completely original. The physics-based interactions introduce an entertaining sense of unpredictability, particularly when unstable constructions collapse or objects are deliberately knocked over. However, the building system is relatively basic, lacking the precision tools and extensive customization options found in more sophisticated construction games.

The ability to alter the appearance of stones adds another enjoyable layer to the creative mechanics. Players can apply different colors to their structures, allowing them to create monuments that are visually distinct from the historically inspired environment. Changing the time of day further enhances experimentation by revealing how lighting affects the appearance and atmosphere of different arrangements. Premade structures offer additional opportunities for exploration and inspiration. These features provide enough flexibility for casual creativity, although the limited selection of construction materials eventually becomes noticeable. Players who enjoy open-ended experimentation may appreciate the simplicity, while those seeking complex architectural simulations could find the available mechanics restrictive.

Movement and accessibility receive considerable attention, with walking, teleportation, and flying available as navigation methods. Having several options is particularly valuable in virtual reality, where comfort and motion sensitivity vary considerably between individuals. Teleportation provides a practical alternative to continuous movement, while flying allows players to examine monuments from elevated positions and appreciate their overall layouts. The introductory tutorial helps newcomers understand the interaction mechanics without demanding extensive familiarity with VR controls. Nevertheless, the experience remains heavily dependent on suitable virtual reality equipment, and some players may still encounter discomfort during extended movement sessions.

Visually, the game benefits from its Unreal Engine 4 foundation, delivering atmospheric lighting and convincing representations of massive stone structures. The surrounding landscape provides a relatively peaceful setting, allowing the monument itself to remain the primary attraction. Sunrise and sunset are especially effective in establishing a sense of place, while the seasonal lighting demonstrations contribute to the educational presentation. However, environmental detail and graphical sophistication are comparatively modest. The world is not particularly expansive, and players expecting richly populated surroundings or elaborate environmental interactions may find the setting somewhat empty. Its visual appeal comes primarily from scale, lighting, and historical atmosphere rather than cutting-edge graphical technology.

The sound design complements the relaxed presentation through informative narration and background music. Historical explanations provide context without constantly interrupting exploration, while the soundtrack supports the contemplative atmosphere. Additional features, including a music player, virtual photography, and the ability to save sandbox creations, give players reasons to experiment beyond the initial guided experience. These conveniences are welcome, but they cannot completely compensate for the absence of meaningful progression systems or substantial gameplay challenges. Once the historical demonstrations have been experienced and the basic construction mechanics explored, there is relatively little structured content encouraging repeated visits.

Steam Deck compatibility is unverified, and the experience should not be regarded as suitable for normal handheld gameplay. Stonehenge VR SANDBOX is designed around virtual reality hardware, including compatible headsets and motion controllers, making a properly configured PC-based VR setup the appropriate way to experience its features. Even if the application could be launched through alternative configurations, that would not establish practical standalone Steam Deck compatibility.

Overall, Stonehenge VR SANDBOX is a worthwhile curiosity for history enthusiasts, educators, and players interested in the creative possibilities of virtual reality. Its educational demonstrations, atmospheric monument recreation, and accessible sandbox mechanics provide a distinctive experience that successfully encourages exploration and imagination. Unfortunately, limited construction depth, minimal structured objectives, and relatively short-lived novelty prevent it from achieving greater longevity. It works best as an interactive historical attraction rather than a conventional game intended for lengthy sessions. For audiences interested in prehistoric architecture and relaxed virtual experimentation, it offers an enjoyable experience despite its limitations. 

It is an imaginative and approachable educational VR experience that deserves recognition for combining historical discovery with creative freedom, even though its limited gameplay variety and reliance on specialized hardware make it better suited to curious explorers than players seeking a substantial, long-lasting adventure.

Rating: 7/10
